summary.headline: Rushil Decor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to INR 2,920 mn, but EBITDA margin was 7.9% and PAT only INR 20 mn amid input cost and freight pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 27.8% YoY, driven by normalised Andhra Pradesh MDF operations and a 65.3% jump in laminate revenue. Gross margin was 39% and EBITDA INR 182 mn (7.9% margin), but profitability was hit by elevated resin/chemical costs, higher freight and West Asia shipping disruption. Management said prices are now sustainable with no further hikes beyond the taken ones, and debt is on a schedule to be cleared around FY29 with no major capex beyond maintenance.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,456 mn (+17.2% YoY), EBITDA INR 123 mn (8.4%). India revenue INR 1,447 mn (+32.9%), India volume 52,162 CBM (+16.1%), realisation INR 27,736/CBM (+14.4%). Capacity utilisation 66% after the April maintenance shutdown; exports subdued at ~255 CBM.

segments.name: Laminate (total)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 736 mn (+65.3%): India INR 251 mn (+60.6%), export INR 485 mn (+67.9%). Volume ~8.8 lakh sheets (+27.9%), blended realisation INR 836/sheet (+29.3%). EBITDA INR 52 mn (7%).

segments.name: Jumbo laminate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 mn (+25% YoY), volume ~1.13 lakh sheets (+20.4%), EBITDA INR 23 mn (20.6%). Management puts utilisation at 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis against 28 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.name: PVC / MDF retail
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 96 mn (+13.1% YoY), volume +6.9%, EBITDA INR 8 mn (7.9% margin).

guidance_outlook: Jumbo laminate utilisation aspiration: ~50-55% in FY27 and 70-75% next year; ~60% utilisation would give ~INR 75 cr revenue, 90% ~INR 140 cr (Phase 1 + Phase 2).

Management expects Jumbo margins to be maintained through the year; existing laminate normal margin cited at 9-10%, combined laminate margin expected above 10% once Jumbo ramps, subject to chemical and war uncertainty.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10-12%; management said realistically 1-2 quarters more to reach it.
MDF utilisation for FY27 expected to exceed FY26's ~75%; internal targets of 50% volume and 60% value from value-added products.
Debt including working capital ~INR 260 cr; scheduled repayment ~INR 55 cr per year, expected to be debt-free around Q2 FY29; only INR 5-10 cr operational capex planned in FY27.
Current MDF exports running at ~3,200 CBM in July vs 4,000-5,000 CBM per month last year; no revenue guidance given for FY27.
capex_capacity: Jumbo laminate capacity 28 lakh sheets (1 mm basis); capex ~INR 90 cr; management cites asset turn ~1.4-1.5x at full potential.
Jumbo utilisation 29% currently, aspiration 55-60% in FY27 (per call; reconcile with 50-55% stated later), 70-75% next year.
MDF capacity utilisation 66% in Q1 FY27 vs 83% in Q4 FY26 (April planned shutdown); FY26 full year ~75%.
Laminate plant had a single-boiler constraint after Jumbo capacity was added in one plant, reducing output in Q1.
No major capex beyond maintenance; operational capex INR 5-10 cr in FY27.
Entered two new export markets (Honduras, Greece); added 15 distributors and 46 retailers/dealers in Q1.
demand_pricing: MDF industry growing at ~20% CAGR; management says ~800 CBM/day of new capacity can be absorbed, but new capacity (organised and unorganised) is adding competition in domestic market.
MDF price hike of ~15% taken and sustained with no discounts; no further hikes after that. Laminate ~10% hike (taken in Q4 FY26) covering inflation; no further hikes.
Resin prices up ~35-40% vs pre-war; wood prices flat; resin easing in July described as 'very marginal'.
MDF OEM share 35-40% of domestic volume; OEM and retail prices currently the same; no fixed-price long-term OEM contracts.
Export MDF held back by container shortage and high freight; orders in hand but customers must approve higher freight before shipment.
Thailand and Vietnam are supplying the West Asia/export demand; 8-10 overseas factories have BIS licences, but no significant imports into India yet.
Laminate domestic volume growth 15-20%; export growth from new Far East customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDF OEM vs retail split and how did it move in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM is 35-40% of domestic volume, rest via distribution and retail; the mix in Q1 was the same as Q4 per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jumbo laminate utilisation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis; capex was ~INR 90 cr for 28 lakh sheets; full-potential revenue ~INR 140 cr at 90% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF volume stay flat YoY and why were exports low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the planned April shutdown, elevated chemical prices causing buyers to hold back, and West Asia disruption; exports were ~255 CBM due to container shortage and high freight.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no hikes beyond 15% (MDF) and 10% (laminate); market will not accept more, so no guidance on further hikes.

qa_highlights.question: When will the consolidated EBITDA margin reach 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration is this quarter, but realistically 1-2 quarters more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to full potential revenue (~INR 1,100 cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 revenue guidance; said laminate normal turnover ~INR 200 cr could reach INR 250 cr and Jumbo will take time, with no guidance given for the total.

risks_watch: Input cost pressure: resin up ~35-40% vs pre-war with only 'very marginal' easing in July; management says the market will not accept further price hikes, so margin recovery depends on resin and chemical prices.
Export volumes: MDF exports ~255 CBM in Q1 and ~3,200 CBM in July vs 4,000-5,000 CBM per month last year, held back by container shortage, high freight and West Asia shipping disruption.

Domestic MDF oversupply: new organised and unorganised capacity adding competition; an analyst raised possible inventory loss if raw material stays elevated and oversupply persists, and management replied 'Maybe yes'.
Jumbo laminate ramp-up: utilisation 29% on a 1 mm-equivalent basis vs 50-55% (or 55-60%) aspiration for FY27; new export markets need certifications and multi-year contracts, so timing is uncertain.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10-12%: management said realistically 1-2 quarters more; laminate normal margin fell to about 5% in Q1 vs 9-10% historically.

Watch Q2 FY27 for MDF utilisation recovery from 66%, laminate margin recovery, whether the 15% MDF and 10% laminate price hikes hold without discounts, and the debt reduction pace (~INR 18 cr repaid in Q1).
key_quotes: So yes, we don't see any negative side of pricing going at this point of time. The prices, you can say, is more sustainable at this point of time.
Now we have done a single boiler unit. So that also was one of the reasons why the production was also less.
But realistically, yes, we may take 1 or 2 quarters more to reach up to that level.
So considering the schedule which we have been given by the banks and the financial institutions, approximately Q2 FY29, we will be able to clear our debt.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on pricing sustainability, debt reduction and the Jumbo laminate ramp, but cautious and often evasive on margin timing, FY27 revenue guidance and further price hikes, repeatedly citing volatile chemical prices and the West Asia situation. Answers on the cause of the 5% laminate margin and the full-potential revenue path were qualified as "too early to say".
